issues.legal_issue: A conviction under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code cannot stand when fewer than five persons are found to have formed an unlawful assembly.

A witness may be contradicted by a prior police statement only by drawing the witness’s attention to the specific relevant passage and proving that passage in accordance with Sections 162 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and 145 of the Evidence Act.
A material omission in a prior statement may amount to a contradiction, but a contradiction or omission discredits a witness only when it is material in the circumstances of the case.

The last-seen-together theory cannot establish an accused’s involvement where the deceased was thereafter in the company of others and the evidence does not place the accused with the deceased near the time of death.

A murder conviction cannot be sustained when the eyewitness testimony is unreliable and the remaining evidence, including last-seen-together evidence, does not prove the accused’s involvement beyond reasonable doubt.
